title: Metric dimension and maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of graph Laplacians
summary: We study equality between metric dimension and the maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. These quantities are not ordered in general. Using the standard decomposition associated with twin classes, we separate forced multiplicities from quotient-spectrum contributions. We give complete equality classifications for complete multipartite graphs and core--satellite graphs, and enumerate the multipartite equality graphs by order. For graphs formed by attaching at least two leaves to every vertex of a connected core, the metric dimension and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $ 1 $ are known; we show that this multiplicity is maximal for both matrices, and uniquely maximal except for $ P_3 $. We enumerate this core--leaf family up to isomorphism and obtain a uniform asymptotic formula by order and metric dimension, together with the quadratic exponential growth rate $ 1/18 $. An exact census of connected graphs of orders two through seven identifies the first separating examples and examples without twins. Finally, for every odd $ r \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3} $, we study $ Θ_{2, 2, r} $ and determine both maximum multiplicities: the two equality properties alternate with $ r $ modulo four, producing infinite separating families in both directions.

title: A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton
summary: We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that $\frac{1-q}{(q^n;q)_m}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}$ has nonnegative power-series coefficients for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. We obtain a polynomial version by bounding a Möbius correction by first differences of Gaussian coefficients. The proof uses partitions and quadratic and cubic semi-invariants of binary forms. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner--Stanton--White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

title: Vertex Removal and Vertex-Edge Domination
summary: A vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ $ve$-dominates every edge incident with a vertex in its closed neighborhood $N_{G}[v]$. A set of vertices is a vertex-edge dominating set ($ve$-dominating set) if every edge of $G$ is $ve$-dominated by some vertex in the set. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the vertex-edge domination number $γ_{ve}(G)$, also known as the isolation number. In this paper, we study the effect of vertex removal on $γ_{ve}(G)$, establish sharp bounds on $γ_{ve}(G-v)$ and characterize the vertices whose removal decreases, preserves, or increases $γ_{ve}(G)$. Let $V^0(G)$ and $V^+(G)$ denote the sets of vertices whose removal preserves and increases $γ_{ve}(G)$, respectively, and let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ consist of the vertices in $V^0(G)$ belonging to every minimum $ve$-dominating set. We prove that \[ |V^0(G)|\geq3|V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)|+\sum_{v\in V^+(G)} \bigl(γ_{ve}(G-v)-γ_{ve}(G)+1\bigr). \] In particular, $|V^0(G)|\geq 2|V^+(G)|$. We also prove that every vertex in $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ lies on a cycle and that $V^0(T)\neq\emptyset$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three.

title: Gaussian Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums in Higher Dimensions
summary: For sequences of $n$ nonnegative integer vectors in $\mathbb Z^k$ with distinct subset sums, we prove, for fixed $k$, the uniform lower bound $M\ge (C_k-o(1))2^{n/k}/\sqrt n$ for the largest coordinate, where \[ C_k=\sqrt{\frac{2k}π}\, \frac{(k+1)^{(k-1)/(2k)}}{\sqrt{\lfloor (k+1)^2/4\rfloor}}. \] The proof compares a Gaussian-kernel expectation with a sum over a translated lattice, uniformly over the vector sequence. We optimise the resulting quadratic-form constant using a vertex second-moment certificate. We show that $C_k$ also exceeds the variance constant obtained by optimising an ellipsoidal geometry.

title: Partitionability is NP-complete
summary: We show that the problem of deciding whether a simplicial complex is partitionable is NP-complete in dimensions two and higher, answering a 1995 question of Kleinschmidt and Onn.

title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
summary: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.

title: Subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs
summary: Since their introduction by Karoński, Scheinerman, and Singer-Cohen in 90's, random intersection graphs have attracted much attention, mostly due to their various applications. In this article, we establish a general result for the probability that a given small subgraph is present in a random intersection graph. Our theorem applies to a broad range of parameters, including regimes that have not previously been considered in the literature. Moreover, it extends known results and situates them within a broader framework, making this approach a convenient tool for comparing the probabilities of graphs in the random intersection graph model. To prove our main result, we develop new proof techniques that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been employed in the study of small subgraphs in random intersection graphs. Many special cases and examples are presented as well.

title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of cliques
summary: Let $X^{(r)}_n$ denote the number of copies of a complete graph $K_r$ in the random intersection graph model on $n$ vertices. We derive upper bounds on the distance between the standardized version of $X^{(r)}_n$ and the standard normal distribution, measured in both the Kolmogorov and Wasserstein metrics. We complement these results with necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality. As a byproduct, we provide precise estimates for the variance of $X^{(r)}_n$. In the process, we develop new general techniques for analysing so--called clique covers, which play a crucial role in the study of subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs.

title: Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings
summary: We study the bipanchromatic number $χ_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $β=χ_P-\lceilα/2\rceil \leq χ_B$, where $χ_P$ is the panchromatic number and $α$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $χ_B=β$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $χ_B/β<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\leα<χ_P$ we show that every integer from $β$ to $χ_P-1$ occurs as $χ_B$ while $χ_P$ and $α$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,χ_P,α$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $α=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,χ_P,α$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2α<|V|$. Finally, we prove $χ_B/L\le5/4$ and $χ_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.

title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
summary: A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $95$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.

title: Total $\{k\}$-domination in caterpillars: Structural properties and exact results
summary: The total $\{k\}$-domination problem ($T\{k\}DP$) seeks a minimum-weight function such that the sum of weights in every open neighborhood is at least $k$. While this problem is known to be NP-hard for general graphs, we demonstrate that for the family of caterpillars, it simplifies to the classical total domination number ($k=1$) via the identity $γ^{\{k\}}_t(G) = kγ_t(G)$. This reduction is supported by a general upper bound established for all graphs, which we prove to be tight specifically for caterpillars. The central tool for our analysis is the introduction of a $(T,R)$-representation, a one-to-one mapping that abstracts caterpillar structure into discrete vectors based on support vertex distribution and central path segment lengths. By characterizing these segments through congruence modulo 4, we derive an exact closed-form expression for the total $\{k\}$-domination number of any caterpillar graph.

title: A Pittel-type limit law for the largest component of random $d$-uniform hypergraphs: enumeration and excursions
summary: Let $H_d(n,M)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $M$ hyperedges. In the critical window $M=\frac{n}{d(d-1)}(1+λn^{-1/3})+O(1)$, its largest component $L_n$ satisfies $$n^{-2/3}L_n\xrightarrow{\mathcal L} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}\bigl((d-1)^{1/3}a,λ(d-1)^{-2/3}\bigr).$$ (Here $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}(x,μ)$ denotes the limiting law of the largest component of the critical random graph established by Pittel (2001).) The proof rests on two pillars. First, a bivariate exponential formula gives the exact finite-size law of $L_n$. Subsequently, cancellation of the orders $n,n^{2/3},n^{1/3}$ in the tree normalization determines the series of rooted hypertrees, then that of unicyclic components and its singular expansions at the radius of convergence $ρ_d$. These calculations are exact; they serve the fixed-excess identities and the cancellation mechanism, and nothing more: no unproved uniformity in the excess enters the proof of the limit law. Next, by exploration and martingale approximation, the ordered sizes converge unconditionally to the excursion lengths of a Brownian motion with parabolic drift. A monotone coupling transfers the law to $H_d(n,M)$. The limit law is then identified with Pittel's law by a Brownian rescaling: if $h=d-1$, it suffices to multiply lengths by $h^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at parameter $λh^{-2/3}$. The exact Poisson representation dispenses with any separate deconditioning. We also formulate a two-regime $d$-uniform Bollobas bound (Wright for fixed $\ell$, global combinatorial beyond that), and explicitly indicate why neither regime alone suffices to close the analytic route.

title: PL standardness of the four-pentachoron census sphere Q
summary: We prove that the four-pentachoron homotopy \(4\)-sphere \(Q\) singled out in the census of Burke, Burton and Spreer is PL homeomorphic to the standard \(4\)-sphere. The key construction identifies the compact exterior of an explicit locally flat \(2\)-sphere in an auxiliary 39-vertex model of \(Q\) with the exterior of Budney, Burton and Hillman, then certifies its fibration by a normal cut followed by a relative collapse. The exterior identification uses finite checked moves, an exact regular-neighbourhood construction and a PL lemma controlling the passage through an ideal triangulation. Cutting the compact exterior along the specified normal hypersurface gives a manifold that collapses onto one boundary copy of the punctured \(3\)-torus in 209,144 elementary pairs; a marked product lemma identifies the cut as a product. The resulting integral monodromy realizes \(Q\) as a Cappell--Shaneson filling whose two surgery framings are standard by Gompf's results. The fibration certificate is independent of Issa's earlier PL-compatible constructions. Combined with the published census, the result establishes standardness for every homotopy \(4\)-sphere triangulated with at most four pentachora.

title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
summary: The induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)$ is defined as the minimum order of a graph $F$ such that any 2-coloring of its edges with red and blue leads to either a red induced copy of $G$ or a blue induced copy of $H$. In 1998, Kohayakawa, Prömel, and Rödl conjectured that for any fixed graph $G$, there exists a constant $f=f(G)$ such that the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G, H)$ is bounded by $|V(H)|^f$ for every graph $H$. In this paper, we completely solve the Kohayakawa--Prömel--Rödl conjecture, which states that for any graphs $G$ and $H$ with $|V(G)|=k\ge2$ and $|V(H)|=t\ge2$, $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)\le t^{60k^2+3}$. This verifies the conjecture with $f(G)=60|V(G)|^2+3$.

title: On Entries of Spectral Decompositions and Applications
summary: The entries of the spectral idempotents of a graph are its local and crossed local multiplicities. This paper uses these classical quantities in three applications. First, in a graph on $n$ vertices without isolated vertices, every local multiplicity is at most $\frac{n-1}{n}$, and every diagonal entry of the Cesaro average mixing matrix is at most $1-\frac{2}{n}+\frac{2}{n^2}$. In both bounds equality holds only for the complete graph. This proves the connected form of the complete graph trace conjecture of Godsil, Guo and Sobchuk together with its equality case, and component and degree refinements follow. The two upper bounds and their attainment by complete graphs also occur in a recent machine checked proof, without a formal characterization of when equality holds. Second, for the line graph of a connected graph $Γ$, the average return probability at a bridge with a bipartite component on one side is at least the reciprocal of the rank of the unsigned incidence matrix. Equality holds exactly for $P_2$ and $P_3$. The proof combines local moments with known inverse-incidence formulas. Finally, the paper gives a short proof of Godsil's entry criterion, which says that vertices $u$ and $v$ are strongly cospectral exactly when $\left|(E_θ)_{uv}\right|=(E_θ)_{uu}$ for every eigenvalue $θ$. The criterion recovers the known classification in connected noncomplete strongly regular graphs, where the strongly cospectral pairs are precisely the two-vertex parts of cocktail party graphs.

title: The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs
summary: The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $χ_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ χ_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $Γ$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.

title: Frozen colorings and recolorability of blowups
summary: The $k$-reconfiguration graph $R_k(G)$ of the proper $k$-colorings of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-colorings of $G$, with an edge between two colorings if they differ on exactly one vertex. A graph $G$ is recolorable if $R_k(G)$ is connected for all $k \ge χ(G) + 1$. In this paper, we study recolorability under blowups through frozen colorings, here blowup means replacing vertices with non-empty cliques. We characterize frozen colorings of a blowup of $G$ in terms of maximal independent sets of the base graph, and develop a lifting principle that transfers suitable frozen obstructions from an induced subgraph to a blowup of the ambient graph. This framework yields several consequences. In particular, we answer negatively a question of Belavadi, Cameron and Sintiari on recoloring via modular decomposition, and disprove their conjecture on blowups of prime graphs. We further determine exactly which cycles have all blowups recolorable: this holds for $C_n$ if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,7\}$. The frozen obstructions arising from the negative cases, together with the lifting principle, imply that if every blowup of a graph $G$ is recolorable, then every induced hole of $G$ has length $4$, $5$, or $7$. Finally, using linear programming duality, we show that every such graph $G$ is fractionally co-strongly perfect.

title: A proof of Vince's conjecture on the average order of connected induced subgraphs
summary: We prove that the average order of connected induced subgraphs of a connected simple graph of order $n$ and minimum degree at least $3$ is strictly greater than $n/2$, which settles a conjecture of Vince~[\emph{J. Graph Theory} 97 (2021), 82--103]. We go further and show that, for connected simple graphs of order $n$ and minimum degree exactly $k\ge3$, $K_k\vee(K_1\cup K_{n-k-1})$ uniquely minimizes this average under additional conditions.

title: On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality
summary: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). Let $U_{n,r}$ denote the rank-$r$ uniform matroid on $n$ elements, where $0<r<n$, and let $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ denote the matroid obtained by replacing each element of $U_{n,r}$ with $q$ parallel copies. They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. In this paper, we prove that every $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ with $q\geq3$ satisfies the inequality. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. For matroids, we further prove that every element of a minimum-size loopless and coloopless counterexample lies in exactly one series or parallel class of size two.

title: Size and spectral radius conditions for the existence of $k$-factor in graphs with given minimum degree
summary: In recent years, characterizing the conditions for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in graphs has received significant academic attention. For integers $b\ge a\ge 1$, an $[a, b]$-factor of a graph $G$ is defined as a spanning subgraph $H$ such that $a\le d_{H}(v)\le b$ for every $v\in V(G)$. If $a=b=k$, a $[k, k]$-factor is called a $k$-factor of $G$. Let $δ(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. Hao and Li [Electron. J. Combin. (2024)] posed the problem of characterizing the size or spectral radius conditions for a graph to contain an $[a,b]$-factor with $δ(G)\ge a$. Fan, Lin and Zhu [Discrete Math. (2026)] solved the size version of this problem for the case $a < b.$ In this paper, for $a=b=k$, we characterize the size condition for a graph to have a $k$-factor with $δ(G)\ge k$. Using this result, we also characterize the spectral radius and distance spectral radius conditions for a graph to have a $k$-factor, respectively.

title: Ehrhart positivity of smooth polytopes with few facets
summary: For each dimension $d$, we determine the minimum number of facets of a smooth $d$-dimensional lattice polytope whose Ehrhart polynomial has at least one negative coefficient. This minimum is six in dimension $d=3$, seven in dimension $d=4$, and $d+2$ in every dimension $d\ge 5$. The lower bounds follow from the classification of smooth lattice polytopes with at most $d+2$ facets, together with explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials in dimensions at most $4$. We also prove that a lattice polytope of dimension at least $3$ with a smooth vertex cannot be $2$-integral with respect to any ordered lattice basis.

title: Almost entropic matroids and $(k,L)$-systems
summary: For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.

title: Functions determining few direction: the final missing case
summary: By results of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme and Szőnyi, and of Ball, if a function $f: {\mathbb F}_q\to{\mathbb F}_q$ determines fewer than $(q+3)/2$ directions, then $f-f(0)$ is linear over a subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$, except possibly when $q$ is even and $f$ determines exactly $q/2+1$ directions. We settle this case: $f-f(0)$ is then additive. Hence every small minimal blocking set of Rédei type in PG(2,$q$) is linear.

title: Intersecting families with large covering number - On a conjecture of Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige
summary: Stability theorems on intersecting families are often formulated via the covering number of set families. Let $M(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ with covering number $t$. It is known that for any fixed $t$ and fixed $k$ sufficiently large relative to $t$, one has $M(n,k,t)=(p_{t-1}(k)+o(1))(k)\binom{n}{k}$ as $n$ tends to infinity, where $p_{t-1}(k)$ is the maximum number of covers of size $t-1$ that a $k$-uniform intersecting family can have provided its covering number is $t-1$. Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured that $p_t(k)=k^t-\binom{t}{2}k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$ for fixed $t$ as $k$ tends to infinity and they also showed that $p_t(k)=k^t-b(t)k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$, where $b(t)$ is defined as the extremum of the following minimization problem. Suppose a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F$ of covering number $t$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal F_1,\dots,\mathcal F_t$ such that for every $i$ there exists a set $X_i$ with $X_i \subseteq F_i$ for all $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$ and the $X_i$'s are pairwise disjoint and non-empty. Then $b(t)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{i=1}^t(k-|X_i|)$ over all such families, partitions and $X_i$'s. In accordance with the conjecture on $p_t(k)$, Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured $b(t)=\binom{t}{2}$ for all $t\ge 2$ and proved $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\lfloor \frac{t-1}{2}\rfloor^{3/2}\le b(t)\le \binom{t}{2}$. In this note, we present a counterexample to the conjecture showing $b(t)\le 2\sqrt2\,t^{3/2}\sqrt{\log t}$ $+O(t^{3/2})$ and improve the lower bound to $\frac{2}{3^{3/4}}t^{3/2}-O(t)\le b(t)$. The counterexample was found by ChatGPT 6.1Sol, the lower bound proof is due to the human author.

title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
summary: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $ρ(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $ρ(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Blažej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $ρ(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $Θ(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.

title: Balanced subgraph counts and quasirandomness: a proof of the Janson--Sós conjecture
summary: For $0<p\leq1$, a graph sequence is $p$-quasirandom if every fixed finite simple graph $H$ has limiting labelled subgraph density $p^{|E(H)|}$. Janson and Sós [\emph{European J. Combin.} (2015)] conjectured that, for every finite simple graph $F$ with at least two edges, $p$-quasirandomness is characterized by the random-graph asymptotics of the symmetrized counts of copies of $F$ across every balanced partition into $|V(F)|$ classes. In this paper, we prove this conjecture for all such $F$, including those with isolated vertices.

title: Fourier Decomposition and E-Eigenvalues of Hypergraph Polynomials over Finite Abelian Groups
summary: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with polynomial $f_H(\bm{x})=\sum_{e\in E}\prod_{v\in e}x_v$. For a finite abelian group $G$ and a subgroup $S$ of $G$, the $k$-partite Cayley hypergraph $K$ has $k$ disjoint vertex parts, each indexed by $G$, and $\{(1,g_1),\ldots,(k,g_k)\}$ is an edge if and only if $g_1+\cdots+g_k\in S$. For $k=2$, $K$ is isomorphic to the Bi-Cayley graph associated with $G$ and $S$. For $k\ge3$, we use character theory to express $f_K$, under a complex unitary change of variables, as a sum of exactly $[G:S]$ nonzero monomials in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. This yields a direct sum decomposition whenever $S$ is a proper subgroup of $G$. When $G=\Z_2^m$, this transformation is real and orthogonal, enabling us to determine the complete sets of complex E-eigenvalues and Z-eigenvalues of the adjacency tensor of $K$.

title: Sharp Euler-factor positivity for the BG-rank-refined five-core crank
summary: In this paper, we complete the resolution of Stanton's problem OPAC--005 by proving its fixed-BG-rank assertion. We further establish a sharp nine-factor positivity theorem for the joint generating function. Let $K_{n,j}(z)$ enumerate partitions of $5n+4$ with BG-rank $j$ by the integer five-core crank prescribed in OPAC--005, and put $[5]_z=1+z+z^2+z^3+z^4$. We prove that $K_{n,j}(z)/[5]_z$ has nonnegative integer Laurent coefficients for every $n\ge0$ and $j\in \mathbb Z$. The refined equidistribution theorem of Berkovich and Garvan gives divisibility; the new assertion is coefficientwise nonnegativity. Set $Ψ(u,z,q)=\sum_{n\ge0}\sum_{j\in \mathbb Z}q^{n+1}u^jK_{n,j}(z)$ and $D(q)=\prod_{d\ge1}(1-q^{2d})$. For every nonnegative integer $M$, we show that $D(q)^MΨ(u,z,q)/[5]_z$ has nonnegative coefficients if and only if $M\le9$. Thus positivity survives after removing nine of the ten partition factors supplied by the core--quotient decomposition. A coefficient equal to $-4$ at $M=10$ proves sharpness. The key step is a compensation between lattice terms of different core sizes that preserves both the BG-rank and the full integer crank. Theta identities and three local coefficient inequalities provide the required nonnegative contributions, and an explicit allocation ensures that none is used twice. The resulting factorization also yields a nine-color convolution and coefficientwise finite-difference inequalities through order nine.

title: On the MDS conjecture in even characteristic
summary: We prove that every nontrivial linear $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) code over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic two satisfies $n\le q+1$, except in dimensions $k=3$ and $k=q-1$, where $n\le q+2$. This resolves the linear MDS conjecture in even characteristic.

title: Secure Domination in Odd-order Sierpinski Graphs
summary: A nonempty vertex set D of a graph is secure if and only if, for every nonempty subset X of D, the closed neighborhood of X contains at least as many vertices of D as vertices outside D. A secure dominating set is a set that is both secure and dominating, and the secure domination number is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Previous work determined the secure domination number of Sierpinski graphs S_n k for even k and for odd k when n = 2. The exact values for odd k and n\geq3 remained open. In this paper, we determine these remaining values.

title: Extremal graphs without cycles of length 0 modulo 4
summary: In a remarkable recent result, Győri, Li, Salia, Tompkins, Varga and Zhu determined the maximum size in a graph of given order and containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of all graphs attaining this maximum. This answers a question posed by Li, Pan and Shi. Very recently, Chu, Park and Ryu established a sharp upper bound on the number of edges in a 2-connected graph containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. We also give a complete characterization of all such graphs attaining this bound.

title: A Complete Dichotomy for $L_\infty$ Permutation Removal
summary: We study the removal problem for permutation patterns under the normalized $L_\infty$ earth mover's distance. We prove a complete dichotomy. Let \[ \mathcal E =\{(12),(21),(132),(213),(231),(312)\}. \] If $σ\in\mathcal E$, then every permutation of length $n$ that is $\varepsilon$-far from being $σ$-free contains at least $\varepsilon(n-1)$ copies of $σ$; for $0<\varepsilon\le 1/16$, this is sharp up to a constant factor for all sufficiently large $n$. If $σ\in S_k\setminus\mathcal E$, then for every sufficiently large $n$ there is a permutation of length $n$ that is $1/(8k)$-far from being $σ$-free and contains exactly one copy of $σ$. Thus the usual positive-density removal conclusion fails for every nontrivial permutation pattern, but the sparse behavior is completely characterized: the minimum number of copies is linear for exactly six patterns and is one for all others. Consequently, no canonical one-sided tester that rejects only after finding a forbidden copy can have query complexity independent of the permutation length.
comment: The results and proofs in this paper have also been formally verified in Lean~4; see the "Formal verification'' section following the main text for details

title: Ordered Trees with Linear Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers
summary: We characterize the following three classes of ordered trees: $\qquad$ (1) trees $T$ satisfying $R_<(T,K_n)=O(n)$; $\qquad$ (2) $χ$-bounding trees; $\qquad$ (3) Ramsey-good trees. In particular, we show that the first two classes coincide. The second characterization answers a question of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt, and the third resolves a problem of Balko and Poljak. In our proof, we also introduce several novel constructions of ordered graphs with sublinear independence number, giving lower bounds on $R_<(F,K_n)$ for various ordered forests $F$.

title: An Erdős-Szekeres-Type Result on Permutation Patterns
summary: We construct an infinite set of patterns $(p,q)$ where $p$ is an almost increasing permutation and $q$ is an almost decreasing permutation, such that the exponential growth rate of permutations avoiding $(p,q)$ is 2. This extends a classical result of Erdős and Szekeres.

title: Avoiding abelian squares with three colours in the continuous setting
summary: An $n$-colouring of the real line is a Lebesgue measurable function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to A$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ colours. An abelian square for $f$ is a finite interval $U\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ where every colour shows up in the left and in the right half of $U$ with exactly the same Lebesgue measure. It is known that every $2$-colouring contains an abelian square. On the other hand, Alon, Grytczuk, Laso{ń}, and Michałek (2009) proved that there exist $4$-colourings that avoid abelian squares, while the question for $3$-colourings remained open. We construct a $3$-colouring that avoids abelian squares, disproving a conjecture of Laso{ń} (2015). However, in contrast to the case of 4-colourings, the set of 3-colourings that avoid abelian squares is meagre. We show this using an argument based on the KKM lemma.

title: On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices
summary: A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of Östergård--Paavola and Ó Catháin--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.

title: Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture
summary: We show that the uniform random $d$-regular graph model on $n$ vertices is, in total variation distance, asymptotically close to the union of $d$ uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, provided that $n$ is even and $ω(1) = d \leq n^{1/10}$. This confirms a conjecture by Hollom, Lichev, Mond, Portier, and Wang for this range of parameters. This result has a couple of interesting consequences. First, this shows that random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exhibit sprinkling properties for some range of parameters, thereby confirming a conjecture by Isaev, McKay, Southwell and Zhukovskii in that range. Second, we give a short alternative proof of the upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture in the sparse regime.

title: Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
summary: Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(π(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $π(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(π(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(π(P)+ε)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(π(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $π_d=π(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)λ_d\leπ_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $λ_d$ is the vertex Turán density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-π_d=\exp(-Θ(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\leπ_2\le2.15121$.

title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
summary: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.

title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
summary: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.

title: Extremal secant size distributions in projective planes
summary: Given a point set $S$ in a projective plane of order $q$, each line $\ell$ determines a secant of size $|S\cap \ell|$. We study how concentrated this secant-size distribution can be. We develop a general framework for estimating and, in several cases, determining the extremal number. We point out how the extremal constructions vary depending on the remainder of the size of the set modulo $q$, and classify several extremal families of point sets, building from concurrent lines, Baer {subplanes} and lines in general position. On the lower bound side, we rely on stability results in the Desarguesian case and applications of the standard equalities in general. Finally, we connect the problem to a novel concept, called general position on level 2 for point and line sets, which then leads to a Sidon-type problem over finite fields called projective Sidon sets, providing an additional arithmetic model for highly concentrated secant-size distributions.

title: Vanishing Uniform Turán Densities: Characterization and Jumps
summary: Uniform Turán density problems ask for the minimum density threshold that guarantees a copy of a fixed 3-uniform hypergraph $F$ in every sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraph whose edges are uniformly distributed. This line of research was initiated by Erdős and Sós in the 1980s, who introduced the notion of \emph{vertex-set Turán density} $π_{vvv}(F)$. Reiher, Rödl and Schacht later defined two related concepts, namely, the \emph{vertex-pair Turán density} $π_{ve}(F)$ and the \emph{cherry Turán density} $π_{ee}(F)$, which satisfy the chain of inequalities $π_{vvv}(F)\geπ_{ve}(F)\geπ_{ee}(F)$. In this paper, we investigate the problem for their vanishing densities. First, we characterize the 3-uniform hypergraphs $F$ for which $π_{ee}(F)=0$, thereby answering a question posed by Schacht. We show that these are precisely the so-called \emph{max-layered} 3-uniform hypergraphs recently introduced by Lamaison. Furthermore, we answer an analogous question of Lamaison for the \emph{minimum-codegree palette density} $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}$. Together, these results imply that the following are equivalent: $π_{ee}(F)=0$, $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}(F)=0$, and $F$ is a max-layered 3-uniform hypergraph. Let $\star \in \{vvv, ve, ee \}$. We say that zero is a \emph{jump} for $π_{\star}$ if there exists $c>0$ such that no $3$-uniform hypergraph $F$ satisfies $π_{\star}(F)\in(0,c)$. A famous result of Reiher, Rödl and Schacht asserts that zero is a jump for $π_{vvv}$. In contrast, we prove that zero is not a jump for either $π_{ve}$ or $π_{ee}$. This also yields a negative answer to Schacht's well-ordering question for $π_{ve}$. Together with existing results, these findings complete the picture for all three notions of uniform Turán density at zero.

title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
summary: For a fixed integer $a>0$, consider the shifted truncations \[ F_{n,a}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!} \] and their monic integral normalizations $P_{n,a}(x)=(n+a)!F_{n,a}(x)$. In this paper, we prove that, for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible has natural density one. We also prove that $G_{n,a}:=\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})$ is primitive for all sufficiently large $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible, and that it contains $A_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. Finally, we prove that, for any fixed integer $a>0$, the discriminant of $F_{n,a}$ is a nonsquare for a density-one set of $n$, and hence that $\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})=S_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. To obtain irreducibility with density one, we use a result of Shorey and Tijdeman, as well as a smooth-number density argument. Following that, two explicitly chosen Newton polygons give cycles that force primitivity, and hence containment of $A_n$. Finally, an exact computation of the valuation of the discriminant at primes satisfying $\frac n2+a<p<n+a$ implies that the discriminant is a nonsquare for odd $a$ and almost all $n$, implying the group is $S_n$ in those cases. For even $a$, we contradict the existence of many square discriminants by showing they generate a family of biased Dirichlet characters. These imply many zeros off of the critical line, which contradict standard zero-density bounds.

title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
summary: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Treviño's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
comment: 11 pages, Lean code formalizing the proofs available at: https://github.com/larryrolen/Spt_Noncongruences_Lean

title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
summary: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2πx)+2\cos(2πy)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.

title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
summary: Let $χ_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,χ_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $ξ_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, Φ_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $Φ_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ Φ_L(u) := \frac{1}{2π}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} ξ_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $ξ_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $Λ_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge Λ_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $Λ_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $Λ_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $Λ_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $Λ_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
summary: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.

title: Quantum Variance for Hecke--Maass Cusp Forms on the Vertical Geodesic
summary: Let $X=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H$, and let $\{u_j\}$ be an orthonormal basis of even Hecke--Maass cusp forms on $X$ with Laplace eigenvalues $1/4+t_j^2$. For a real-valued $ψ\in C_c^\infty(0,\infty)$, define \[ μ_j(ψ)=\int_0^\inftyψ(y)|u_j(iy)|^2\,\frac{dy}{y}, \qquad M(ψ)=\frac6π\int_0^\inftyψ(y)\,\frac{dy}{y}. \] For $T\ge2$, $1\le U\le T$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove \[ \sum_{\substack{u_j\ {\rm even}\\T<t_j\le T+U}} L(1,\mathrm{sym}^2u_j)|μ_j(ψ)-M(ψ)|^2 \ll_{ψ,\varepsilon}T^{1+\varepsilon}. \] As a consequence, for fixed $0<θ\le1$, $0<η<θ/2$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, if $T^θ\le U\le T$, then all but \[ O_{ψ,θ,η,\varepsilon} \!\left(T^{1+2η+\varepsilon}\right) \] of the even forms with $T<t_j\le T+U$ satisfy $μ_j(ψ)=M(ψ)+O(T^{-η})$. In particular, the exceptional proportion tends to zero in this short spectral interval.

title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
summary: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.

title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
summary: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.

title: On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation
summary: We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.
comment: 15 pages. Comments welcome. This paper significantly extends the results of arXiv:2606.02620 by the same author

title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.

title: Small values of the Riemann zeta-function near the critical line
summary: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we study negative moments and small values of the Riemann zeta-function to the right of the critical line. For every fixed $0<k<1/2$, we establish the conjecturally sharp bound $$ \frac1T\int_T^{2T} \Big|ζ(\tfrac12+α+it)\Big|^{-2k}\,dt \ll α^{-k^2}, $$ for $α=o(1)$ and $α\gg 1/\log T$. We also obtain almost sharp upper bounds slightly to the left of $1/\log T$. This improves the upper bounds of the first two authors for shifts as small as $1/\log T$, confirming a conjecture of Gonek in this range. A separate bound for the moment at $k=1/2$ yields an improved bound for cancellation in the Möbius function. Namely, we show that $$ \sum_{n\leq x}μ(n) \ll \sqrt{x}\exp \bigg(C\sqrt{\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}}\bigg) $$ for some $C>0$, improving on previous results of Soundararajan, Balazard and de Roton, and of the first two authors. For $t$ chosen uniformly from $[T,2T]$, we also prove that \[ \min_{|h|\leq1} \Big|ζ\Big(\tfrac12+α+i(t+h)\Big)\Big| =α^{1+o(1)} \] in probability, provided that $α\ll (\log T)^{-c}$ for some fixed $c >0$, and $α\log T/\log\log T\to\infty$. This agrees with the leading order predicted by a minimum analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating Conjecture. Further results include bounds for minima on intervals of logarithmically growing length, for negative moments in almost all short intervals, and an extension of the range of sharp negative-moment bounds for $k>1/2$. A main ingredient in the proof of some of these results is a Gaussian large-deviation upper bound for $\log|ζ(1/2+α+it)|^{-1}$, obtained by building on work of Arguin, Bailey, and Roberts.

title: A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
summary: We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.

title: Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions
summary: For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $ω(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leqω(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.

title: New Directions in Irrationality
summary: Since Apéry's proof of the irrationality of $ζ(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Apéry as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $μ(ζ(2))<4.62675$ and $μ(ζ(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,ζ(3),ζ(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $μ(Aζ(3)+Bζ(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.
comment: 73 pages: 35-page main text; 17 figures. Code sources: https://github.com/RamanujanMachine/new-directions-in-irrationality

title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindelöf-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
summary: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.

title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
summary: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.

title: Theta Relations
summary: Motivated by the classical quartic and cubic theta identities, we establish a product formula for Siegel--Jacobi theta series associated with rationally isometric positive-definite quadratic spaces. Our main theorem expresses a product of theta series of arbitrary Siegel degree as a finite double character sum over quotients of commensurable lattices. For the root lattice $A_2$, it yields a finite Fourier identity for cubes of cubic theta functions, a new proof of the two-variable cubic identity, and seven independent relations in degree two. A second specialization gives a new square analogue of the two-variable cubic identity. At the origin it reduces to $a(q)a(q^2)=b(q)b(q^2)+c(q)c(q^2)$; in degree two, the same seven relation patterns recur with each cube replaced by the corresponding product at $τ$ and $2τ$. We further extend the cubic identities on $A_2$ to $\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq3$, and to $2\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq2$, in arbitrary Siegel degree. The doubled-order construction recovers Jacobi's quartic identity and gives its analogues in arbitrary Siegel degree.

title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
summary: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.

title: Uncountably many settled elements are never Frobenius elements
summary: Boston and Jones conjectured that given a number field $K$, a quadratic polynomial $f\in K[x]$, and an element $α\in K$ such that the arboreal Galois representation $ρ_{f,α}:\text{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$ attached to the pair $(f,α)$ is well defined, any element in the image of such representation that is a Frobenius for an unramified prime of $K$ is a settled element. We exhibit an explicit uncountable subset $S\subseteq \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$, consisting of pairwise non-conjugate settled elements, such that no matter how $K,f,α$ are chosen, no element of $S$ can be a Frobenius for any ramified or unramified prime of $K$.

title: On the average of class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms
summary: We prove that the sum of class numbers of primitive indefinite binary quadratic forms with integer coefficients over positive nonsquare discriminants less than $X$ is $O(X^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log X}/(\log X)^{3/2})$. This improves the longstanding classical upper bound $O(X^{3/2}/\log X)$ and implies the same upper bound for the corresponding sum over real quadratic fields. Our main input is a uniform upper bound for the number of small fundamental solutions to Pell's equation. In particular, we prove that, for almost all nonsquare positive integers $D$, the fundamental solution $\varepsilon_D$ of $t^2-Du^2=1$ is larger than any fixed power of $D$.

title: Irrationality exponents of logarithmic numbers: Values, quotients, and graded approximation
summary: We establish degree-dependent irrationality-exponent bounds for logarithms at algebraic arguments and sharper bounds when conjugate logarithms match. A two-torus construction gives an upper bound of three for ratios of logarithms of multiplicatively independent positive rational numbers. We also treat normalized quadratic logarithms and circular logarithms. The rational-logarithm and rational-power exponent-two cases were treated earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang; we retain them within the broader framework and its Lean verification. Starting from the interpolation and determinant method in OpenAI's September 24, 2026 preprint on the irrationality exponent of $π$, we track the arithmetic cost of algebraic embeddings and the effects of matching conjugate logarithms. A second, graded Pade construction gives near-optimal measures for powers and bounded-degree polynomial values at sufficiently small logarithmic arguments, with estimates uniform in both coefficient height and rational denominator. We state the branch, independence, parameter-order, and approximation-field hypotheses explicitly. The Lean supplement has reviewed endpoint correspondences for all 62 numbered results: 53 direct checked endpoints or compositions, and nine applications with named classical theorem inputs. Native proofs of those inputs and separate formalizations of every unnumbered assertion are not supplied. Appendix A gives the exact declarations, hypotheses, and verification evidence.

title: Simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets
summary: Visibility from the origin in integer lattices is a well-studied problem. More recently, the corresponding question for cut-and-project sets has attracted attention. We consider simultaneous visibility, which asks what points in a set are visible from every point of another set. This question was studied for the integer lattice by Rearick and Rumsey, among others. In this work, we investigate simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets associated with real quadratic fields satisfying the Hammarhjelm condition. Under suitable geometric conditions on the finite set, we prove that the density of the simultaneously visible points exists and derive an explicit formula for it. We also examine simultaneous visibility in more general cut-and-project sets under a condition on the associated lattice.

title: Euler systems for self-dual Hecke characters over biquadratic fields with applications
summary: We construct a new Euler system attached to a self-dual Hecke character $χ$ over an imaginary biquadratic field $K_0$. The Euler system is anticyclotomic in the sense of Jetchev--Neková{\v r}--Skinner. As arithmetic applications, we deduce instances of the Bloch--Kato conjecture in analytic ranks $0$, $1$, and $2$ (the last one for certain CM abelian surfaces). In addition, we establish the full Iwasawa--Greenberg main conjecture for $χ$ over $K_0$. In this biquadratic setting, our work generalizes Rubin's work on the Iwasawa main conjectures for imaginary quadratic fields using Euler systems of elliptic units, while complementing known results of Hida and Hsieh for general CM fields.

title: Simultaneous popular differences for polynomial and linear progressions in finite fields
summary: We study simultaneous popular differences for polynomial progressions and linear progressions over finite fields $\mathbb F_p$. For certain families of polynomial progressions of algebraic complexity $1$, such as $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^3, x+2y^3)$, we prove the existence of $y \neq 0$ which is popular simultaneously for both progressions. This extends previous results by Conlon, Dong and Hong who considered complexity $0$ progressions. On the other hand, we construct counterexamples showing that simultaneous popular differences are not guaranteed to exist for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^2, x+2y^2)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y, x+3y)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x,x+y,x+2y,x+3y)$, answering questions posed by Conlon, Dong and Hong.

title: A necessary condition for a Romanoff type theorem
summary: Let $\{a_k\}_{k\ge1}$ be an infinite strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with $a_k\mid a_{k+1}$ for every integer $k\ge1$. Dai and Pan proved that the set of integers of the form $p^2+q^2+a_k+a_l$, where $p,q$ are primes and $k,l\ge1$, has positive lower asymptotic density if $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log a_k}{k}<\infty$ and $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d<\infty$. They also asked whether the latter condition is necessary. In this paper, we show that this condition is necessary by proving that if $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d=\infty$, then this set has asymptotic density zero.

title: A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions
summary: We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $Ω(n)$ and $Ω(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Teräväinen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $ω$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.

title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits\ for Positive Factorial Multiples
summary: Let $τ(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ τ(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.

title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
summary: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.

title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
summary: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $θ=β/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $Nθ\toγ>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/θ$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $γ$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $β$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $γ\to\infty$.

title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
summary: We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erdős--Rényi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.

title: Solid-angle formulas for simplicial cones and random shifted sections of polytopes
summary: We consider simplicial cones $C = \operatorname{pos}(v_1, \ldots, v_n) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose generators have a Gram matrix of the form $(\langle v_i, v_j \rangle)_{i,j=1}^n = \operatorname{Id}_n+\sum_{j=1}^p λ_j u_j u_j^T$, where $p\in \{0,\ldots, n\}$, $λ_1, \ldots, λ_p > -1$ and $u_1,\ldots, u_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are orthogonal unit vectors. We derive an explicit $p$-dimensional integral formula for the solid angle of $C$ involving the analytic continuation of the standard normal distribution function. As an application, explicit formulas are obtained for the expected face numbers of sections of acute orthocentric simplices and crosspolytopes with uniformly distributed linear subspaces translated by a fixed vector. The translation vector is assumed to lie outside the affine hulls of all proper faces of the polytope. All solid angles entering these formulas are expressed as integrals of dimension at most two. This application includes regular simplices and regular crosspolytopes as special cases.

title: Berry--Esseen Bounds for Faces in Unimodular Triangulations of Random Polytopes
summary: Consider the number of faces arising from unimodular triangulations of random polytopes associated with Erdős--Rényi graphs. Focusing on two-dimensional faces of regular unimodular triangulations of random symmetric edge polytopes, we derive precise asymptotic expansions for the expectation and variance and then establish a quantitative central limit theorem with an explicit Berry--Esseen bound. The proof combines an algebraically derived characterization of faces in terms of local graph configurations with a detailed combinatorial--geometric study of the relevant configurations. The normal approximation is established using the discrete Malliavin--Stein method. We also determine the asymptotic orders of the expectation and variance and establish a quantitative central limit theorem for the number of faces in each fixed higher dimension. These results identify a common local mechanism underlying the fluctuations of face numbers and extend the distributional theory of random symmetric edge polytopes [Donzelmann et al., arXiv:2603.10650] beyond edge statistics.

title: On $c$-Normal Maximal Chains of Sylow Subgroups in Finite Groups
summary: Let $G$ be finite group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be $c$-normal in $G$ if there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that $G = HN$ and $H\cap N\leq H_G$, where $H_G$ is the core of $H$ in $G$. Let $P$ be a nontrivial $p$-group. A chain of subgroups $1=P_0 <P_1<\cdots P_{n-1}<P_n=P$ is called a maximal chain of $P$ provided that $|P_i:P_{i-1}|=p$ for $i=1,2,\ldots n-1$. In this paper, we determine the structure of finite groups having $c$-normal subgroups of of a maximal chain of Sylow subgroups. We obtain new characterizations of finite $p$-nilpotent and supersolvable groups.

title: Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups
summary: We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input. The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.

title: Ordered frequency in relatively hyperbolic groups
summary: We study word frequencies along infinite strings whose finite prefixes lie in a regular language of geodesic representatives of group elements. Let \((G,\mathcal H)\) be a non-elementary relatively hyperbolic pair, and suppose that, over a finite symmetric generating set, there is a prefix-closed regular language containing exactly one shortest word representing each element of \(G\). Modeling this language using a finite-state Markov chain, we define a probability measure on the space of infinite strings whose finite prefixes are words belonging to this language. Each such string labels a geodesic ray emanating from the identity. We show there is a continuous surjection from this space onto the Bowditch boundary, and the pushforward of the probability measure under this map is a Patterson--Sullivan probability obtained as a weak limit of weighted counts of group elements. For a word \(w\), the ordered frequency of \(w\) along a given labeled ray is the limiting proportion of consecutive nonoverlapping tuples of length \(|w|\) that exactly spell \(w\). For almost every infinite string under the constructed measure, these frequencies exist simultaneously for all nonempty geodesic words, with no restriction on their lengths. Consequently, almost every boundary point with respect to this Patterson--Sullivan probability is the endpoint of at least one such ray along which all these frequencies exist. In particular, after possibly enlarging the generating set, these results apply when the peripheral subgroups are virtually abelian.

title: Linear $2$-Group Actions With Exactly One Regular Orbit
summary: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-group and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then the characteristic $q$ of $V$ is a Fermat prime, $V$ is irreducible over ${\Bbb F}_q$, ${\rm dim}_{{\Bbb F}_q}V$ is a power of $2$, and the centraliser of $G$ in ${\rm GL}(V)$ embeds into $G$. For every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ we determine the largest orbit size $2^{x_m}$ of a Sylow $2$-subgroup $P_m$ of ${\rm GL}_{2^{m-1}}(q)$ on its natural module $V_m$, and the number of orbits of this size, which is $1$, $2$, or $3$. Our main result is that for every Fermat prime $q$ and every $m\ge 1$ there is an irreducible subgroup of $P_m$ of order $2^{x_m}$ that has exactly one regular orbit on $V_m$. In this respect $p=2$ behaves like $p=3$, and unlike the Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ studied in an earlier paper. The proof places a group related to a Singer cycle into every block of $q-1$ coordinates. This reduces the problem, for all Fermat primes at once, to a question about subgroups of a Sylow $2$-subgroup of a symmetric group acting on subsets, which we answer by means of fibre products. We also determine which largest orbits occur in two small levels, and we classify the examples in some small cases with the help of a computer.

title: Maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems
summary: We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. To obtain the upper bounds, we use the cubical flat torus theorem of Wise and Woodhouse. We then verify the sharpness of these upper bounds by constructing free abelian subgroups of the corresponding ranks. Our result shows that the maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of ordinary cactus groups can be larger than conjectured by Genevois. As an application, we show that these groups are not quasi-isometric to any right-angled Artin group unless they are virtually free abelian.

title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
summary: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups $C_W$ associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems $(W,S)$. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of $C_{W_T}$ for some spherical subset $T\subseteq S$. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types $B$, $D$, $E$, $F$, and $H$, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine $C_{W(I_2(p))}$ directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When $S$ is finite, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups of $C_W$. In type $A$, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group $J_n$ if and only if it embeds into a Sylow $2$-subgroup of the symmetric group $S_n$. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types $A$ and $B$ and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.

title: Finite groups with large sum of element orders compared to cyclic groups
summary: For a finite group $G$ let $ψ(G)$ denote the sum of the orders of elements in $G$. If $G$ has order $n$ then, by a result of Amiri, Jafarian Amiri and Isaacs, $ψ(G)\leψ(C_n)$, where $C_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. We determine all finite groups such that $ψ(G)\ge\frac{1}{3}ψ(C_n)$.

title: Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable
summary: Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.

title: Wielandt subgroups of nilpotent residuals and Fitting-height bounds
summary: For a finite group $G$, let $\mathrm W(G)$ be the intersection of the normalizers of the nilpotent residuals of the subnormal subgroups of $G$, and let $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ be the length of the associated upper series. Thus $\mathrm W(G)=G$ exactly when all these residuals are normal in $G$. We prove that every finite soluble group satisfies $\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)\le h(G)\le4\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Fitting height, and that $h(G)\le3\ell_{\mathrm W}(G)$ if $|G|$ is odd or the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $G$ are abelian. Both constants are attained at every length, the constant $4$ by $\{2,3\}$-groups. Moreover, every pair $(n,h)$ with $n\le h\le4n$ occurs as $(\ell_{\mathrm W}(G),h(G))$. The constant $4$ comes from primitive groups. A soluble primitive group $V\rtimes M$ satisfies $\mathrm W(V\rtimes M)=V\rtimes M$ if and only if every abelian subgroup of $\mathrm F(M)$ is cyclic. It then has Fitting height four if and only if $\mathrm F(M)=C\times Q_8$, with $C$ cyclic, and $M$ induces the full group $\mathrm{Out}(Q_8)\cong S_3$. We also determine when the base group of a soluble regular wreath product is the first term of the series.

title: Determinant characters and multiplicative solubility of finite skew braces
summary: Let $B$ be a finite skew brace. We prove that if the additive derived subgroup $(B,+)'$ is nilpotent, then the multiplicative group $(B,\cdot)$ is soluble. In particular, this holds for finite skew braces with supersoluble or metabelian additive group.
